chosen: tasks ['joint_embedding', 'retrieval', 'cross_modal_prediction']; primary retrieval; modalities ['image', 'expression']; predict expression from image
rationale: retrieval: retrieval; joint_embedding: joint embeddings; cross_modal_prediction: prediction of gene expression from histology

Samples come in 8 'patient' groups; 'patient' explains 77% of the variance of the top expression components; neighbouring samples are spatially correlated (median Moran's I 0.14). Samples within a group are not independent, so whole groups are held out: grouped 4-fold cross-validation, each group tested exactly once, with one further group per fold held out for validation (early stopping and model selection).

The objective needs a shared space (joint_embedding, retrieval, cross_modal_prediction) and there are about 8,511 training pairs. Contrastive alignment learns that space directly from the pairing: each sample's partner is its positive and the other samples in the batch its negatives (InfoNCE, a lower bound on the mutual information between modalities).
Highest screening score among 4 candidates (alignment_recall_at_10 0.087 on held-out screening samples). Screened on 2000 training and 500 validation samples from separate groups.
Each patch covers the spot's own footprint (145 px), the tissue its RNA was captured from; resized to the encoder's input size.
28% of the variance in mean image colour lies between groups (ICC >= 20%); a frozen encoder would encode stain/scanner differences as signal. Colour statistics are matched to the training data.
'expression' is a matrix modality; no pretrained encoder applies, so a small MLP is trained on the preprocessed features.

chosen: library-size normalisation to the median library size, then log1p; top 2,000 variable; pca
rationale: genes matrix, 83% zeros, median library 3,231 (integer counts): library-size normalisation to the median library size, then log1p; keep the 2,000 most variable features (fitted on training folds only); then PCA to 100 components (fitted on training data): about 8,511 training samples for 2,000 features is < 5 per feature, so compressing first reduces parameters and count noise.

About 8,511 training pairs: a 256-d joint space with 2-layer heads (512 hidden) is small relative to n; batch 512 gives 511 negatives per positive; early stopping on validation (patience 15) and a 180s cap per fit; temperature learned from 0.07.

Frozen pretrained backbones with small trainable projection heads: few trainable parameters for the number of pairs (low variance), features computed once. Fine-tuning not tried: no pre-aligned dual encoder among the chosen encoders.

First measurable task in the objective is 'retrieval'. Every metric is computed on held-out data and compared with unimodal features, linear alignment (CCA), ridge regression and chance, to show whether integration helped.

chosen: 1 samples lack one of the paired modalities and are not used for alignment
rationale: Recorded while drawing the folds.

Patient explains 77% of the variance in expression PCs (group silhouette 0.63), and 36 slides are nested in 8 patients. Holding out whole patients is the only way to keep held-out data independent. Four folds (2 test patients each, 1 validation patient) leave about 8.5k training pairs per fit and fit the max_folds=4 limit. Budget: 4x(180+135+135) + 180 refit + 4x180 critic = 2700 s, exactly the total.

phikon is best on every screening metric: recall@10 0.087 (next best 0.063), ridge R2 0.215 (next best 0.184) and probe F1 0.43 (next best 0.39). Pretraining was on TCGA tiles, not on these spot patches. Because there is no zero-shot baseline, any corpus overlap could only make the frozen features slightly optimistic, not the reported baselines. With about 8.5k pairs from only 5 training patients per fold, frozen features with small heads are the low-variance choice.

decision: adopt soft InfoNCE + regression, with hard InfoNCE as a comparison
rationale: 23.2% of expression spots have a near-twin, so hard negatives would often be false negatives. The objective explicitly asks for prediction of expression from histology, which justifies the regression term. The labels are not named in the objective, are only 23% present and stay evaluation-only (no supervised_ce).

These are the two least certain choices. Soft targets depend on a near-twin threshold. Patch size matters because spot spacing is 1.88x the diameter, so a 2x patch adds context from the gaps between spots, and expression has spatial autocorrelation (median Moran's I 0.14) that context may capture. Together they use the remaining budget exactly.

decision: keep retrieval recall@10 as the primary metric; keep prediction Pearson as secondary
rationale: Retrieval is the first measurable task in the objective. Pearson on the top 50 genes, measured against ridge and CCA, covers the prediction goal. Group silhouette tracks how much patient effect is left in the joint space.

The primary works but its scores are low. Its validation mean recall@10 is 0.0335, about 6x chance (≈0.0054). It beats CCA (0.0179) in 4/4 folds, by +0.016 ± 0.008. For image-to-expression prediction it only ties ridge: Pearson on the top 50 genes is 0.150 vs 0.152, and the primary is better in just 2/4 folds. The automatic flag calls hard_infonce's gain on recall@10 'within noise', but it beat the primary in every fold: +0.0043, +0.0041, +0.0084, +0.0101 (mean +0.0067, SD ≈0.003). patch_context_2x was also better in 4/4 folds, by less (+0.0025). The soft-target loss was chosen because 23% of spots have near-twins, but the evidence goes against that choice. On the same folds, hard InfoNCE gave higher recall@10 for every held-out patient group, by about 20% relative (0.040 vs 0.0335). A paired comparison over four folds gives t ≈ 4.5, which is small evidence but consistent. Switching needs no extra compute: the per-fold results already exist and already beat the primary. One caveat: all scores are best-epoch scores picked on validation, so they are slightly optimistic, but that bias is the same for both configurations. Training curves show early peaks (best epochs 3–10) in every configuration, and hard InfoNCE overfits faster (train loss falls to about 1.6 while validation scores drift down). Early stopping already copes with this.
